- When sentiment is consistently low or negative (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use 2-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.6) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to prevent overbought bias.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.6), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 3-period rolling average to anchor forecast near recent mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window; apply linear decay correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per 5-day interval after day 10.
- If sentiment history shows strong divergence (e.g., sentiment spikes but price doesn’t follow), model may misinterpret sentiment; use sentiment as a multiplier (0.8–1.2) to adjust forecast magnitude.
